text: What if Earth had rings, like Saturn?
Step outside, and a giant arch would stretch right across the sky.
At night, it would still catch sunlight. So nights would be a lot brighter.
But rings cast shadows. In winter, a wide strip of Earth would sit in the shade, and get colder.
Then there's space. Rocks in the ring would smash into any satellite that crossed it.
And the rings wouldn't last forever. The Moon tugs at them, the rocks keep crashing, and some could fall and burn up as shooting stars.
So could Earth ever have rings? Here's the strange part. It might have had them already.
Some scientists think Earth had a rocky ring four hundred and sixty-six million years ago. Its shadow may have helped cool the planet.
So tonight, look up. That plain sky might once have had a ring.
